name: Belarus
summary: Red over green with a vertical red and white ornamental band at the hoist. Adopted after a 1995 referendum, it is based on the flag of the Byelorussian SSR. The historical white-red-white flag is widely used by the opposition.
origin: The Belarusian People's Republic of 1918 and independent Belarus from 1991 used a white-red-white horizontal flag. In 1995 President Alexander Lukashenko held a referendum on new state symbols; voters approved a design adapted from the Soviet-era flag, without the hammer, sickle and star.
The ornament was slightly modified in 2012. The white-red-white flag became the main symbol of the opposition, especially during the 2020 protests.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The Soviet era and the blood of those who fought in wars, including the Second World War.

colors.name: Green
colors.meaning: Hope, the forests and fields of Belarus.

symbols.name: Rushnyk ornament
symbols.description: A vertical band of red on white traditional embroidery patterns at the hoist.
symbols.meaning: Belarusian folk culture; the pattern is based on a 1917 design by Matrona Markevich called 'The Rising Sun'.

facts: The white-red-white flag is banned from public display in Belarus in many contexts.
Flag, Emblem and Anthem Day is the second Sunday of May.
The ornament is one of the few textile patterns on any national flag.
clues: Red over green with a red and white ornamental band at the hoist.
Adopted after a 1995 referendum, replacing a white-red-white flag.
Its hoist band reproduces a traditional embroidered towel.
